visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the projectile-motion setup with axes, parabolic path, launch components, and correct flight time placement, whereas Lesson 2 uses a generic archer/trajectory aesthetic with confusing or meaningless numeric markings that do not correctly represent the given physics quantities.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 has a clearly wired, functional fill-in checkpoint after act_decomposition with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and feedback, whereas Lesson 2 provides no gate specs or plan at all, so it has no demonstrable interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 provides clear, well-paced narration with spoken math rendered naturally, while Lesson 2 has no transcript available and therefore cannot demonstrate any narration quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed cues that generally align with the narrated references to vectors, trajectory, decomposition, vertical/horizontal focus, and range, whereas Lesson 2 has no transcript or cue timing available, making its visual-narration synchronization absent and therefore worse.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly explains projectile range via velocity decomposition, vertical flight time, and constant horizontal motion with the right numerical result, whereas Lesson 2 has no available transcript or script to demonstrate any accurate or pedagogically useful explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a much more polished, full-frame visual style with large legible text and cohesive graphics, while Lesson 1 is plainer, less balanced, has small/dim labels, visible player UI, and a diagram pushed low/left with excess empty space.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents strongly preferred it, all with very high confidence, for visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and conceptual accuracy. These dimensions indicate that Lesson 1 accurately represents the projectile-motion setup, includes functional learner interaction, provides clear narration, aligns visuals with narration, and teaches the physics correctly. Lesson 2 was preferred only for polish, with lower confidence, due to its more refined visual style, but that advantage is outweighed by its lack of demonstrated transcript, timing, interactivity, and physics explanation.
